assumptions.reason: spec references '1 tick' for stop offsets but does not define the tick size for this instrument; $0.01 is the standard US equity minimum price increment

assumptions.choice: use abs(entry_price - stop_price) as risk-per-share for both long and short sizing
assumptions.reason: the literal formula (entry_price - stop_price) is negative for shorts since the stop is above entry, which would make the <=1% constraint meaningless; absolute value preserves the intended risk-based sizing purpose for both directions

assumptions.choice: floor to whole shares via math.floor
assumptions.reason: spec gives a sizing inequality but not a rounding rule; whole-share floor is the standard convention that also guarantees the risk constraint is satisfied, not exceeded

assumptions.choice: submit the entry as a market order, then on its Completed notification submit a separate opposite-side Stop order at the stored stop price (a manual 2-leg entry+stop bracket)
assumptions.reason: backtrader's native buy_bracket/sell_bracket always creates a 3rd take-profit leg requiring a limit price, which the spec never defines; the manual 2-leg chain implements exactly 'entry + stop' as stated without inventing a take-profit level

assumptions.choice: when the manual close-price exit condition fires, cancel any still-pending protective stop order before submitting the market close
assumptions.reason: spec requires only one open trade/exit at a time; canceling avoids a conflicting duplicate exit order when both exit conditions could otherwise fire

assumptions.choice: no forced end-of-day close was added; positions may be held across sessions until the exit condition or stop-loss triggers
assumptions.reason: spec describes an intraday reversal signal but never states an explicit end-of-day flatten rule, and canonical defaults prohibit inventing extra exit conditions

assumptions.choice: no additional time-of-day filter was added
assumptions.reason: the harness's single data feed already consists solely of regular-session 5-minute AAPL bars, so the spec's 'ignore signals outside market hours' instruction is satisfied by the feed itself

assumptions.choice: entry orders are submitted as standard market orders in next(), which backtrader fills at the following bar's open, not the signal bar's close
assumptions.reason: the harness provides a standard (non cheat-on-close) Cerebro/broker setup, so an order placed after evaluating the close of bar N cannot literally execute at that same close price; this is the closest achievable literal implementation in this environment
